meta.description: Design Engineer: I design and build interfaces for complex products, with AI in the workflow and inside the product.

servicios.titulo: I design and build digital products.
servicios.intro: I work across product, design and frontend. I can take a feature from definition through implementation and iteration.

items.titulo: I take features from definition to production.
items.texto: I map the flow, design it in Figma and build it with React and TypeScript. Working across both sides lets me make design decisions with implementation in mind from the start.

items.titulo: I build and maintain design systems.
items.texto: I work with tokens, components and documentation to keep design and implementation consistent.

items.titulo: I design and build AI features inside products.
items.texto: I work on both the user experience and the integration of the feature with the model.

items.titulo: I work with dashboards, tables and dense workflows.
items.texto: In these interfaces, information hierarchy, states and clear actions are especially important.

comoTrabajo.titulo: Design and code, with AI in the process.
comoTrabajo.intro: Design Engineer is the title that fits my work best. I work across design and frontend, from defining an experience to implementing it. AI is also part of my day-to-day workflow.

bloques.titulo: I design in Figma and build in code.
bloques.texto: Working across both sides lets me make design decisions with technical constraints in mind, and technical decisions with the original design intent in mind.

bloques.titulo: I use AI assistants every day.
bloques.texto: I use Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini to explore alternatives, write and review code, document decisions and reduce repetitive work. AI helps me iterate faster while product and design decisions remain mine.

Inside the platform I work on. Using AI tools is one thing; designing features that incorporate models is another: what the user sees, how incorrect responses are handled, how long they wait and what the experience costs.

sistema.titulo: A small system, built to scale.
sistema.intro: This site doesn't use a CSS framework. It runs on its own system, using the same principles I apply when working with design systems.
sistema.problema: A growing product or site faces the same challenge: when every section defines its own colors, spacing and behaviors, consistency starts to break as the system grows.
como: Tokens for color, typography, effects and motion.
Reusable components to keep the different sections consistent.
Visual states defined at the system level so their meaning stays consistent.
Shared rules for responsive behavior, instead of solving each section from scratch.
sistema.resultado: Adding a section means reusing the system instead of defining new styles from scratch. The site also serves as a practical example of how I think about and build systems.
sistema.cota: tokens and components, across the site

dalle.contexto: A full-stack AI image generator: type a prompt and get an image. Built end-to-end to explore OpenAI's DALL·E model on a modern MERN stack.
dalle.desafio: Wire a deep-learning image model into a responsive web app — handling generation, cloud storage and a clean create flow.
proceso: Built the MERN stack from scratch: Node.js + Express API, MongoDB persistence, React front end
Integrated OpenAI's DALL·E model to generate images from text prompts
Stored generated images on Cloudinary; styled the interface with Tailwind
Split the deployment: backend on Render, frontend on Vercel
dalle.resultado: A working, deployed image generator — try it live.

tms.contexto: A full brand and web redesign for an engineering consultancy — logo, typography and a responsive marketing site in both desktop and mobile formats.
tms.desafio: Refresh the company's identity and ship a fast, smooth site that feels as polished on mobile as on desktop.
proceso: Redesigned the logo, mailing signatures and client presentation into one cohesive identity
Built the responsive site in React + Gatsby, styled with SCSS
Added Locomotive Scroll for smooth, interactive navigation; served media through Cloudinary

metabaseq.contexto: Batuta is the cybersecurity SaaS platform by Metabase Q. As Frontend Engineer & UX/UI Designer I own its end-to-end frontend experience — from defining the UX in Figma to shipping accessible, high-performance interfaces in production.
metabaseq.desafio: Turn complex security workflows into interfaces that are fast, consistent and genuinely usable, while keeping a growing multi-module platform coherent.
proceso: Define requirements, user flows and technical constraints together with product and engineering
Design and maintain a scalable UI / design system in Figma for consistency across the platform
Build high-performance, accessible interfaces in React, TypeScript, Tailwind and Material UI
Drive product discussions and feature prioritization, improving usability across modules
metabaseq.resultado: Owning both UX and implementation closed design-to-development gaps, standardized components for a more consistent UI, and sped up feature-delivery cycles.
